content.title: Visual hierarchy
content.text:
Imagine three messages: a page title, regular body text, and a small note. If every message uses exactly the same color and emphasis, the page gives the eye fewer clues about what matters.

A useful rule: use color with a reason. “Make it orange because orange looks cool” is not a design explanation. “Make the action easy to notice” is.

content.question: Which is the stronger engineering choice?

options.text: Use a very light text color on a very light background because subtle is always better.
Choose text and background values that remain readable and match the role of the content.
Use as many colors as possible so every element is unique.
Let the browser pick the colors.

feedback.correct: Readable contrast is part of interface quality, not a finishing touch.
feedback.incorrect: Readable contrast is part of interface quality, not a finishing touch.
